$about: PHASE A — can the Base UI branch build and pass its gates, and what does the
full migration cost. Branch experiment/base-ui, 10 August 2026. Nothing
THE HEADLINE: the site BUILDS. `next build` prerenders all 441 pages, and
`gate:html` produced data for the FIRST TIME on this branch — 442 documents
graded. VERDICT.md's 'the site cannot be built' is now definitively false; it
was the unported context-menu, as COMPARISON.md's audit predicted.
The gate run also found a defect class NOTHING else in this project could
see, and it is a Base UI capability gap, not a wiring slip. It is recorded at
full weight below rather than quietly patched, because a green build bought
by hiding a gap is worse than a red one.

gate_status.$note: Order is `pnpm run verify`'s. Each gate run to completion, including the two after the one that halts the chain.
gate_status.gate:test: PASS — 33 files, 580 tests in packages/ui; blocks 91, website 61, core 25, gate 26, theme 13
gate_status.gate:registry: FAIL — and it is unfixable in this working tree, see registry_gate_is_a_commit_artifact
gate_status.gate:smoke: PASS — 107/107 items copied into a bare project and type-checked as a consumer receives them. The brief's expectation confirmed.
gate_status.gate:html: FAIL — 442 documents graded, 12 violations, all one rule, all one component. Was 98 on the first run.
gate_status.honest_summary: Five of six gates are green or green-but-for-a-commit. The sixth is down from 98 violations to 12 and the residue has one named cause.

registry_gate_is_a_commit_artifact.mechanism: gate:registry is `node scripts/build-registry.mjs && git diff --exit-code registry.json`. It asks 'is the committed registry.json current with the source?'. The migration changed the source, so the regenerated file necessarily differs from HEAD.

generator_is_correct.method: ran the generator three times; md5 of registry.json identical across all three (50edb615e70514f2c5904ed15097051c)

registry_gate_is_a_commit_artifact.bucket: not a failure of the migration — it goes green the moment registry.json is committed alongside the source

triage.$legend: Every failure seen this round, in one of the brief's three buckets.

our_bug.symptom: gate:types failed at the FIRST gate: TS7006, parameter 'spec' implicitly has an 'any' type
our_bug.cause: a sibling added `packageOf` as a standalone arrow in a checkJs .mjs; unlike the inline callbacks around it, it has no contextual type
our_bug.fix: JSDoc `@param {string}` per the idiom already in no-css-modules.mjs, plus `?? spec` for the noUncheckedIndexedAccess `parts[0]`, which is truthful rather than an assertion

our_bug.severity: HIGH — this one deleted content from the served bytes and still exited 0
our_bug.symptom: every tab rendered aria-selected="false"; no panel was selected; the SELECTED PANEL'S CONTENT WAS ABSENT from the server render. On the docs site that removed every component demo from the HTML, which is how it surfaced: inject-evidence.mjs could not find [data-lumo-demo-root].
our_bug.cause: React Aria selected the first tab when given no key. Base UI's Tabs.Root also defaults — to the NUMBER 0, an INDEX — but Lumo's Tab maps `id` onto Base UI's required `value`, so tabs are identified by name and 0 matches nothing.
our_bug.fix: derive the first Tab's id in the Tabs wrapper and pass it as defaultValue

the_second_bug_inside_the_first.$note: The first fix used `child.type === Tab` and silently did nothing on the site while passing in jsdom. Worth recording because it will recur for anyone walking children in this library.
the_second_bug_inside_the_first.cause: when a SERVER component composes <Tabs><TabList><Tab/>, those elements are created in the react-server module layer, so each child.type is a CLIENT REFERENCE, not this module's Tab function. The layers are separate module graphs and references resolve per element as React renders it — strictly after the parent's body runs.
the_second_bug_inside_the_first.evidence: the install tabs (composed inside a client component) selected correctly in the same build; the preview tabs (composed in page.tsx, a server component) did not
the_second_bug_inside_the_first.final_fix: match on PROPS, which survive the boundary: TabList requires `label`, a Tab is identified by `id`

our_bug.tests_added: packages/ui/src/tabs.test.tsx — 8 tests, SSR tier. Tabs had NO suite on either engine, which is why this reached a production build.

half_migrated.symptom: served HTML was `<label>` with no `for` beside `<input>` with no name — 4 of the original 98 gate violations
half_migrated.cause: form.tsx's `Label` is still React Aria's AriaLabel, which wires htmlFor through RAC's LabelContext. Nothing provides that context here, because the control beside it is Base UI's NumberField.Input.
half_migrated.fix: thread an explicit id — number-field renders the Label itself, so the wrapper can

half_migrated.symptom: THE 12 REMAINING GATE VIOLATIONS. `<button role="combobox">` with no accessible name, on every Select that uses a visible <Label> instead of aria-label.
half_migrated.cause: same unported form.tsx Label as number-field
half_migrated.why_not_fixed_here: STRUCTURAL, and it is the finding worth carrying. In number-field the WRAPPER renders the Label, so it can thread an id in. In Select the CONSUMER renders it — `<Select><Label>…</Label><SelectTrigger/></Select>` — so there is no seam to inject through without either cloning children or making form.tsx's Label context-aware. The real fix is porting form.tsx's Label onto Base UI's Field.Label, which touches every field component in the library and is the off-ledger item COMPARISON.md flagged as 'form.tsx's Label must learn to emit htmlFor'.
half_migrated.estimate: one focused change to form.tsx plus a re-check of every component that renders a Label; not attempted this round because it is an API-shaped decision, not a wiring fix

half_migrated.finding: half-migrated.json's hunt found 10 further files mixing a react-aria-components runtime import with a rebuilt sibling, and NONE of them throws or renders wrong. The throwing class was exactly two files (context-menu, alert-dialog), both now native, and the predicate was never 'mixes engines' — it was 'renders a Base UI part outside its Base UI Root'.
half_migrated.confirmed_this_round: the full build agrees: 441 pages prerender with those ten files in the tree

capability_gap.severity: HIGH — WCAG 4.1.2, and invisible to every tier except gate:html
capability_gap.what_base_ui_cannot_do: produce an accessible name for a Field-labelled control in a SERVER render

mechanism_read_from_the_installed_dist.route_1: utils/useRegisteredLabelId.js — the label publishes its id into the labelable context inside `useIsoLayoutEffect`. Layout effects do not run on the server.
mechanism_read_from_the_installed_dist.route_2: internals/labelable-provider/useAriaLabelledBy.js — the fallback that scans the DOM for an associated <label> is ALSO in a layout effect.
mechanism_read_from_the_installed_dist.consequence: both of Base UI's naming routes are inert during SSR, so `labelId` and the fallback are both undefined and the control renders with neither aria-labelledby nor aria-label

capability_gap.why_a_wrapping_label_does_not_save_it: Base UI exposes `<span role="checkbox">` / `role="switch"` / `<button role="combobox">` as the control. A native <label> names only labelable ELEMENTS; a span carrying a role is not one. React Aria's hidden real <input> was, which is why the baseline had no such defect.

measured.rule: named-controls (100% of them — no other rule fired)

capability_gap.workaround: `aria-labelledby` passed as a PROP is the one naming route Base UI resolves during render — useAriaLabelledBy reads it ahead of both effects. `useSsrLabelId` in base-ui-adapter.ts mints one id and threads it to the label and the control.
capability_gap.cost_of_the_workaround: per-component, in the shipped source, forever — and it must be re-checked on every Base UI upgrade, because it is compensating for an internal implementation choice rather than using a public seam

does_this_reopen_the_decision.answer: it is evidence for the ledger, not on its own a reversal
does_this_reopen_the_decision.for: this is the SAME defect class VERDICT.md credited Base UI for AVOIDING on axis 1 — React Aria's useSlotId clearing in a layout effect that never runs on the server. Base UI has the same disease in a different organ, and arguably a worse form: a dangling idref is a broken reference, an unnamed control has no name at all. Axis 1 was scored 'Base UI wins' on a count that did not include this, because the site had never been built and the gate had never run.
does_this_reopen_the_decision.against: it is fully workaroundable at the wrapper layer and 86 of 98 instances are already fixed; React Aria's equivalent required a 27KB binary patch of a dependency
does_this_reopen_the_decision.what_it_definitely_does: it removes 'zero dangling idrefs / clean SSR' as a Base UI advantage that can be asserted without qualification, and COMPARISON.md's axis-1 row should be re-scored against gate:html data rather than the 13-component harness

capability_gap.finding: Base UI's AlertDialog.Root is Dialog.Root in alert-dialog mode, and everything the role means lives in that root's store. Lumo's public API already spent the root (DialogTrigger) and the popup (DialogModal) on the plain dialog, so AlertDialog.Root has nowhere to go.
capability_gap.what_it_costs_today: outside-press dismissal stays ON — the exact behaviour the component's own docblock forbids — because the mode that forces disablePointerDismissal is unreachable
capability_gap.status: OPEN — needs a public API decision (an AlertDialogTrigger/Overlay/Modal trio), which this experiment may not make
capability_gap.bucket_note: listed as a capability gap only in the frozen-API sense: Base UI CAN do this correctly, but not through Lumo's current public surface

capability_gap.finding: Base UI's context-menu anchor is a virtual object with getBoundingClientRect(), not a node, so the old `[data-lumo-context-menu-anchor]` assertion has nothing to query. Nothing now verifies that the menu opens AT THE POINTER.
capability_gap.status: TEST COVERAGE DEBT, recorded rather than faked. jsdom computes no layout; this needs a browser tier Lumo does not have.
capability_gap.not_papered_over: the assertion was deleted with a comment saying exactly this, and the vacuous companion assertion (anchor is null after close — now unconditionally true) was deleted too rather than left looking like coverage

tests_restated_not_weakened.$rule: Six tests failed because they asserted React Aria's attribute names or React Aria's DEFECTS on components deliberately re-engined. Each was restated to the property the test existed to protect. Three are strictly stronger. One loses coverage and says so.
tests_restated_not_weakened.toggle.data-selected→data-pressed: React Aria's data-pressed was TRANSIENT pointer-down and data-selected was ON; Base UI spells ON as data-pressed and emits no transient. Verified the variants style the same attribute and aria-pressed agrees. A second test added for the OFF state, so an always-on attribute cannot pass.
tests_restated_not_weakened.overlays.Dismiss×2: STRONGER. Asserted exactly 1 and exactly 2 unreachable English 'Dismiss' sentinels — a budgeted React Aria leak. Base UI emits none, so both now assert the empty set.
tests_restated_not_weakened.overlays.data-has-submenu: STRONGER. Was a styling hook that told a screen reader nothing; now asserts aria-haspopup="menu" and aria-expanded, which is what actually reaches assistive tech. Verified no live selector styles the old attribute.
tests_restated_not_weakened.controls.slider-rtl: React Aria computed the offset in JS and wrote physical `left: 60%`. Base UI writes logical `inset-inline-start: 40%`. Asserting only that would be WEAKER (an LTR track emits 40% too), so the test also pins the direction-derived centring translate — 50% on fa-IR, -50% on en-US — and a second test added for the LTR arm so the flip cannot be a constant.
tests_restated_not_weakened.context-menu.anchor: the one real loss; see the capability_gap entry.

migration_unit_costs.$sources: assembled from the four siblings' JSON, not re-derived

state_selector_rewrites.note: ~7 of every 10 state utilities in the library have to be rewritten, not renamed — the subject moves as often as the name does. The date family's 44 utilities are excluded from 179 because they are authored fresh, not migrated.

date_family_hours.arithmetic_ports_free: @internationalized/date is standalone; PersianCalendar verified with no React present
date_family_hours.family_estimate_days: 18–30 at parity, and the calendar-based members are the expensive end. Estimate, not a measurement; the parity gap is 16 behavioural props plus paste/IME/AT behaviour jsdom cannot test at all.

half_migrated_file_count.note: the honest half-migrated count is 1 FILE — form.tsx — with a blast radius of every component that renders a Label.

off_the_component_ledger: form.tsx's Label must emit an association Base UI can use at SSR — the blocker for select and the largest remaining known item
provider.tsx gains a DirectionProvider and the duty to keep three levers agreeing
build-registry.mjs — DONE, subpath-aware externals and shared companions, gate:smoke 107/107
a browser tier, for the pointer-position and hydration claims jsdom cannot make

what_this_round_did_not_cover: No browser rendered anything. Every claim here is about served bytes and jsdom.
Hydration was not tested. The unnamed-control gap SELF-HEALS on hydration, so a hydration-tier suite would show it clean — that is precisely why it needed the HTML gate.
The 12 remaining violations are the only ones the gate can see. Components with no demo page are ungraded by construction.
Bundle weight was not re-measured after the state-selector rewrite or the naming fix.
gate:registry cannot pass without a commit, so 'all six green' has not been observed in one run and is inferred for that one gate.
